sentences.text: Shri Ghanshyam Pandey, learned counsel for the applicant.
Shri Akshay Namdeo, learned G.A. for the respondent/State.
Shri G.S. Pandey, learned counsel submits that previous counsel i.e. Shri U.K. Tripathi has no objection if he is arguing and appearing in this case.
Shri Ghanshyam Pandey, learned counsel appeared on behalf of the applicant has also filed a Vakalatnama today.
The prayer is allowed.
Office is directed to henceforth reflect the name of counsel Shri Ghanshyam Pandey in place of Shri U.K. Tripathi, on behalf of the applicant in the cause list.
Heard on the question of admission.
Revision is admitted for hearing.

Also heard on I.A. No.10547/2018, an application for suspension of sentence and grant of bail to the applicant.
The revision has been preferred by the applicant against judgment dated 23.06.2018 passed by learned Ist Additional Sessions Judge Bhopal, District Bhopal in Criminal Appeal No. 104/2015 whereby the learned Appellate Court has dismissed the appeal and affirm the judgment and conviction order dated 16.05.2015, passed in Criminal Case No.24/2010, passed by Presiding Judge,
JMFC Sohagpur, District Hoshangabad (M.P.).
Applicant stands convicted for an offence punishable under Section 7 (1)(2)(3) read with Section 16(1)(a)(i) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (2 counts) and has been sentenced to undergo SI for 6 months with fine of Rs.1000/- in default of payment of fine additional S.I. for 1 month.
Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is in jail.
He further submits that there is fair chance to succeed in the case.
The final hearing of this revision will take time.
If the applicant is not released on bail, purpose of filing this application will be frustrated.
Therefore, the application filed on behalf of the applicant may be allowed and the period of his remaining jail sentence may be suspended and he may be released on bail.

sentences.text:
After having heard rival submissions at length, looking to the facts and circumstances of the case,
but without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, I am of the considered opinion that it would be appropriate to suspend the custodial sentence awarded to the applicant and grant bail to him.
Consequently, I.A. No.10547/2018 is allowed subject to deposit of fine amount, if not already deposited.
The custodial sentence awarded to the applicant shall remain suspended during the pendency of this revision.

Applicant Basant be released from custody subject to his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.30,000/- (Rupees Thirty Thousand Only) with one surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court.

The applicant shall appear and mark his presence before the Court of C.J.M.,
Hoshangabad on 10.12.2018 and shall continue to do so on all such future dates as may be given in this behalf, during pendency of the matter.
List the revision for final hearing in due course of time at its own turn.
C.C. as per rules

. 
(RAJENDRA KUMAR SRIVASTAVA) JUDGE sp Basant vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 30 July, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/63355222/
